name: Vectorworks
tagline: Professional 2D drafting, 3D modeling and BIM software for architects, landscape designers and entertainment production.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Vectorworks is a decades-old CAD/BIM package sitting on top of a commercial solid modeling kernel, and that is not something an agent writes in a session. The hard parts are not the UI: they are robust NURBS and solid booleans, constraint solving, parametric objects that survive editing, DWG and IFC round-tripping, and printable sheet layout that a contractor will accept. You can absolutely get an agent to build a pleasant 2D drafting canvas with snapping, layers and dimensions, and that is genuinely useful for a floor plan or a lighting plot. What you cannot get is the part where the file opens correctly on someone else's machine, or the part where the geometry does not quietly go non-manifold. If your actual job depends on this output, the licence is cheaper than the bug hunt.
coreLoopDIY: A local 2D drafting app: draw lines, rectangles, arcs and polylines on a scaled grid with snapping, layers, text and linear dimensions, then export SVG, PDF and DXF.
requirements: A modern browser, everything runs locally
Node for the dev server and build
Willingness to hand-draft instead of using parametric walls, doors and symbols
whatYouLose: Any real 3D: solid modeling, booleans, NURBS surfaces, sections cut from a model
BIM data, parametric objects, and the schedules and reports that come from them
DWG, DXF and IFC fidelity good enough to hand to a consultant or a fabricator
Industry libraries: door and window objects, plant databases, lighting fixture symbols with data
Sheet layout, title blocks, viewports and plotting that reliably prints to scale
moatNotes: The geometry kernel and forty years of edge cases are the product. The ribbon and the icons are the cheap part.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the output has to leave the building. A drawing set goes to a client, a consultant, a planning office or a shop floor, and everyone downstream expects a file format, a scale, a layer convention and a level of precision that only mature CAD reliably produces. Add the object libraries, the plug-in objects other people in your discipline already rely on, and years of your own templates and symbols, and switching cost alone justifies the subscription. A homemade drafting tool is fine for thinking. It is not fine for issuing.
notes: A drafting canvas is a weekend; a CAD kernel is not. The moat is the solid modeling engine plus the file formats everyone downstream already assumes you can produce.
prompt:
Build a local-first 2D drafting app called "Draftpad". No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable: Vite + TypeScript + React for chrome, and a single HTML5 canvas for the drawing surface. State in Zustand. IndexedDB via idb for persistence. No backend, no server, no API keys, so no .env is needed.

Model: a document has a paper size (A4, A3, A1, Arch D), a drawing scale (1:50, 1:100, 1:20, 1/4" = 1'), units (mm or feet-inches), and an ordered list of layers. Each layer has a name, color, line weight, visible flag and locked flag. Entities: line, polyline, rectangle, circle, arc, text, and linear dimension. Store all geometry in real-world units, never pixels.

Editing: pan with space-drag or middle mouse, zoom to cursor with wheel. Tools bound to keys: L line, P polyline, R rectangle, C circle, A arc, T text, D dimension, M move, O offset, X trim, ESC cancel. Snapping to endpoint, midpoint, intersection, center, perpendicular and grid, with a visible snap marker and a toggle per snap type. Orthogonal lock on shift. Typed coordinate and length entry in a command bar at the bottom.

Selection: click, shift-click, rubber band. Move, copy, rotate, mirror, delete, and a properties panel for layer, line weight and line type. Undo and redo with a full history stack, at least 100 steps.

Output: export SVG and print-to-PDF via the browser at correct scale with a simple title block, plus a minimal DXF R12 writer covering LINE, LWPOLYLINE, CIRCLE, ARC and TEXT on named layers. Save and load a .draftpad JSON file.

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt: 3D, solids, NURBS, parametric walls or doors, constraint solving, BIM data, IFC, DWG read or write, external references, multi-user editing.

Ship a README that states plainly what this is not: it is a drafting scratchpad, not a CAD system, and DXF output should be checked before anyone builds from it. Include a seed document with a small floor plan so the app is not empty on first run.
